title: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case

input.lead: The girl was covered in sores, severely dehydrated and had "paper-thin skin" when she was treated
input.summary: The girl was covered in sores, severely dehydrated and had "paper-thin skin" when she was treated
input.evidence_text: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, The 19-month-old girl was less than half the weight a child should be on average for her age By Jonny Humphries North West Published 2 hours ago An "incredibly emaciated" and starving baby, covered in sores, was taken to hospital in a critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, a review has found. The 19-month-old girl weighed 9.7lb (4.4kg) - less than half the 24lb (11kg) expected for an average child of her age - when she was treated in February 2025. A Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, reported the girl was severely dehydrated, had no fatty tissue noted on her body and had "paper-thin skin". The case was closed despite warnings her mother, who was 17 when the baby was born, was neglecting her daughter and had avoided social workers and health visitors for weeks. The CSPR, which referred to the girl as Child K1, said she displayed "skin breakdown" across the "entirety" of her bottom and nappy area. Expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall said medics found "wasting to the buttocks" and open pressure sores extending along her back, hips and bottom. She wrote: "Child K1's presentation of hypothermia, hypoglycaemia [low blood sugar], severe malnutrition, dehydration along with renal failure, evidenced by severe abnormality of blood salts, could have led to death if it had not been identified and emergency treatment initiated." Anonymous tip The review found the baby's mother had struggled with anxiety and low mood since the birth, and had been relying heavily on her own mother to care for the child. title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife

input.lead: A World War Two air raid shelter has been turned into a haven for wildlife with Trafford Council calling the work 'inspirational'
input.summary: A World War Two air raid shelter has been turned into a haven for wildlife with Trafford Council calling the work 'inspirational'
input.evidence_text: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters and drinking stations for insects and animals beside it Work at the site in Urmston, Greater Manchester, has been made possible with the help of local businesses "It's been absolutely thriving with wildlife, said Lisa Smith, allotment treasurer. "We've even had a fox up there. It's just been such an incredible achievement to create this." Smith added: "Since World War Two, pollinators have been under threat due to the loss of 97 per cent of wildflower meadows in the UK, so we thought we really need to try and rectify that." Mick Heery, chairman of Brookfield Allotment, told BBC Radio Manchester sustainability also plays an important role in their work

input.evidence_text: Rudy’s Pizza Napoletana has confirmed it will be bringing its relaxed dining experience and renowned Neapolitan pizzas to Salford for the first time, with a new restaurant opening in Monton village this autumn. To celebrate, the pizzeria is giving away 3,000 pizzas on the house a The new pizzeria, located at 237-239 Monton Road , will transform the former Bennetts Furnishers store that has been vacant since 2022, with work now officially underway. The spacious venue will mark Rudy’s 41st restaurant to date Since launching in Manchester’s Ancoats in 2015, Rudy’s has grown into one of the UK’s most loved pizzerias, celebrated for its light, double fermented dough and unwavering dedication to true Neopolitan craft Testament to its authenticity, Rudy’s is the largest organisation in the world to be accredited by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana (AVPN), the international body that protects and promotes traditional Neapolitan pizza making Rudy’s has also been recognised among the World’s 50 Best Pizzeria, ranking 23rd globally for 2025. Each pizza, from the classic Margherita to the fiery Calabrese, is made to AVPN standards using traditional techniques and ingredients sourced directly from Italy To claim one of 3,000 complimentary pizzas, Monton locals can sign up via this link , where they will be able to choose from Rudy’s favourites such as its Cinghiale , Margherita Con Bufala, and Triple Pepperoni to enjoy at the new opening this summer
